{{MultipleIssues|citation|moresources}}
[[File:ExecutorBattle-SWM.jpg|300px|thumb|Warfare in space]]
'''Space warfare''' or '''space combat''' was the use of armed [[Starship/Legends|starships]] and other spacecraft for the purposes of military actions across [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] and [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. Along with [[Ground warfare/Legends|ground warfare]] and [[Starfighter combat/Legends|starfighter combat]], by [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] space warfare was one of three most significant branches of warfighting. Evolving from [[Water/Legends|water]] [[Navy/Legends|navy]] engagements and in turn the earliest orbital battles, space warfare became a high technology affair that often defined the outcome of the galaxy's most important conflicts.

==Technology==
[[File:DSTurbolaser.png|thumb|left|250px|[[Turbolaser/Legends|Turbolasers]] were the primary form of capital ship armament for thousands of years.]]
Technological innovation determined the design of warships and naval doctrine and the outcome of battles. While the sizes and capabilities of starships varied, four main technologies drove and were advanced by space warfare: weapon systems, shield technology, sublight propulsion, and hyperdrive technology.

===Weaponry===
There were two basic types of space weaponry: energy and conventional. Energy weapons began with [[Maser|microwave lasers]] for offense and were typically secondary to conventional, physical weapons. From [[4000 BBY/Legends|4000 BBY]] however, energy weapons were the dominant form of weaponry in space combat, dominated by the [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolaser]] and the [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannon]], outgrowths of [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] technology that had matured at the same time. On capital ships, energy weapons were normally grouped into batteries based upon the weapon type and its placement upon the hull. For example, on an [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] the heavy turbolasers on the portside of the hull's dorsal surface would be grouped into one battery, while those on the starboard dorsal surface would be grouped into a second battery. [[Targeting computer/Legends|Targeting computers]] in capital ships were usually shared between the weapons of each battery, allowing the gunners to concentrate their fire on particular targets. Other designs of energy weapon included the [[Charric/Legends|charric]], a [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] advancement of early microwave lasers; the [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannon]], an electromagnetic weapon used to non-destructively disable electronic systems; and the [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]], a [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] development that was an immensely more-powerful design of laser that could cause planetary-scale damage.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

===Shield technology===
[[File:N-1_Shields.png|thumb|right|250px|A deflector shield envelops a [[N-1 starfighter/Legends|Naboo starfighter]].]]
[[Deflector shield/Legends|Deflector shields]] were a critical component in starship design and were used to mitigate damage from impacts. They included [[Ray shield/Legends|ray shields]], which protected against energy weapons, and [[Particle shield/Legends|particle shields]], which repelled physical objects. Both types consumed large amounts of energy and for a long period in galactic history, were reserved for only the largest warships with the greatest power-generating capability. Early warship captains therefore thought in terms of [[Armor/Legends|armor]] for defense. Other early defenses included charged particle clouds to diffuse energy weapons and hulls treated with [[Kiirium/Legends|kiirium]] to reflect beams.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

A refinement of the [[squintpipe process]] in the 7500s BBY produced shields that were stronger and quicker to regenerate, and also reduced the effective size of [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|deflector shield generators]]. From then on, reliable deflector shields could be fitted to ships of all sizes.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

In spite of the necessary elements of deflector shields in starship designs, not all ships incorporate them. A notable example of ships lacking deflector shields are the TIE-series starfighters, in particular the TIE/LN starfighter, which was not included alongside life-support systems because Imperial doctrine dictated that their usage among fighter pilots was a sign of cowardice.<ref name="Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>

===Propulsion technology===
[[Sublight engine/Legends|Sublight drives]] propelled ships below the speed of light and were best represented by [[Ion engine/Legends|ion drives]]: powered by [[Fusion generator/Legends|fusion generators]], these engines expelled particles at a very high speed to provide propulsive force. Sublight engines determined speed and maneuverability and could prove decisive: the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN starfighter]] used an extremely efficient [[Twin ion engine/Legends|twin ion engine]] design and stripped-down spaceframe to improve its mobility. The [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] countered this with the faster and more maneuverable [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor/Legends|RZ-1 A-wing interceptor]], which the Empire countered in turn with the even faster [[TIE/IN interceptor/Legends|TIE/IN interceptor]].

[[Hyperdrive/Legends|Hyperdrive]] technology was an enormous influence on strategy in space warfare: fleets travelling faster-than-light in [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] had to traverse known [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]] to avoid dangerous [[Mass shadow/Legends|mass shadows]]. For much of galactic history, starships lacked the computing power to calculate safe routes between systems and were confined to jumps within networks of [[Hyperspace beacon/Legends|jump beacons]]. In war this allowed navies to effectively pin ships at a certain point by disabling its beacon. By [[4100 BBY]], [[Navigation computer/Legends|navigation computers]] had advanced to the point that jump beacons were no longer needed, making control of routes more difficult, as blockading one route merely pushed ships to one of many alternative ones. However, statistically speaking, only a few of these route could be traversed quickly, and a military force that controlled the fast routes could rapidly redeploy to intercept an adversary using the slow ones. Hyperlanes thus determined the strategic geography of space warfare, and fleets repeatedly battled over the same planets on significant hyperspace routes, such as [[Chazwa/Legends|Chazwa]], or planets at hyperlane junctions such as [[Yag'Dhul/Legends|Yag'Dhul]] or [[Brentaal IV/Legends|Brentaal IV]]. Militaries might also maintain secret hyperlanes to get the drop on their enemies: during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] made use of a secret route through the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]] to directly attack [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], while the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|CIS]] negotiated with the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]] for control of the [[Nexus Route/Legends|Nexus Route]] connecting each other's core territories. The Rebel Alliance also made use of secret [[Claatuvac Guild/Legends|Claatuvac Guild]] routes supplied to them by [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] for [[hit-and-hype raiding]] against the Empire.<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref><ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

==Ship classes==
Ships designed for war were typically split into two broad classes: [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] and [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]].

===Starfighters===
{{Main|Starfighter/Legends|Starfighter combat/Legends}}
[[File:Head2Head_AORCR.png|thumb|left|250px|An X-wing and TIE Interceptor in head-to-head combat]]
Starfighters were small craft typically piloted by one or two beings. Their operations and role encompassed an entire doctrine and form of warfare in its own right, known as [[Starfighter combat/Legends|starfighter combat]]. Types included ''space superiority fighters'', [[Bomber/Legends|''bombers'']], and [[Snubfighter/Legends|''snubfighters'']]. Space superiority fighters were stripped-down ships, usually minimally armed and armored, and were used to combat enemy bombers but typically could not attack capital ships. Bombers were more heavily-armed starfighters and were usually equipped with bombs, torpedoes and missiles so that they could make [[bombing run]]s on enemy warships. They were typically less-maneuverable than space superiority fighters and usually required their own fighter escort to avoid being shot down.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

[[Snubfighter/Legends|Snubfighters]] sat between space superiority fighters and bombers in size and armament and were designed to both dogfight with other fighters and attack capital ships. Though snubfighters like the Rebel [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing]] and [[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|Y-wing]] became famous, for the majority of galactic history snubfighters were not heavily used in deep-space combat: commanders considered it better to operate snubfighters from [[Planet/Legends|planet]]-based surface airfields to strike through cloud cover and launch torpedo strikes and strafing runs against attacking ships and troop transports. However, the advantages of snubfighters tended to disappear in the great ranges between opposing fleets and their payloads were not as great as dedicated bombers. It was only after the success of [[N-1 starfighter/Legends|N-1 starfighters]] against [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] battleships at the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], an experience confirmed by the role of Y-wings against the [[Malevolence/Legends|''Malevolence'']] at the [[Battle of the Kaliida Nebula/Legends|Battle of the Kaliida Nebula]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], that the snubfighter began to be taken seriously as a deep-space battleship killer.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

Starfighters may or may not have had a hyperdrive; if not, they were often launched from a carrier or other larger craft. Some, like Imperial [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN starfighters]], were armed only for fighter-on-fighter combat; more versatile ones, like the Rebel [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing]] and [[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|Y-wing]] snubfighters, were also capable of anti-ship and anti-surface attacks. Bombers like the [[TIE/sa tactical bomber/Legends|TIE/sa bomber]] and the [[A/SF-01 B-wing starfighter/Legends|A/SF-01 B-wing starfighters]] were typically poor dogfighters and relied on heavy shielding or escorts to push through fighter screens and attack warships.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

By nature, a starfighter was intended to be small, fast and agile, designed to operate either on its own or as part of a [[Squadron/Legends|squadron]] or a [[Fighter wing/Legends|fighter wing]] on a variety of mission profiles, ranging from escort duty to reconnaissance missions and full-scale assault. Due to their size, starfighters could not engage in self-sufficient operations for any long period of time, needing a base of operations to provide fuel, repairs and supplies for the [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]], given as these cannot be carried aboard in any large quantity.

===Capital ships===
{{Main|Capital ship/Legends}}
A dizzying variety of capital ship classifications existed throughout galactic history. However, all agreed that a capital ship was a military starship that was at least one hundred meters in length. After the Clone Wars, the most common classification system was the [[Anaxes War College System/Legends|Anaxes War College System]], which replaced the system instituted after the [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Ruusan Reformation]]. The largest class recognized by that system was the [[Cruiser/Legends|cruiser]], reflecting the Ruusan Reformation's restriction on transgalactic warships larger than six hundred meters. By the time the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] broke out, many rich [[Sector/Legends|sectors]] had commissioned much larger warships with local-range hyperdrives for their defense, with lengths of several kilometers and making the cruiser an increasingly-meaningless class.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

[[File:Close_Range_Combat_AoRCR.png|thumb|right|250px|An ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer and Mon Calamari cruiser engage each other at point-blank range]]
Under the Anaxes War College System, ships smaller than one hundred meters were classified as either ''starfighters'', or if they were unarmed, [[Transport/Legends|''space transports'']]. Mindful of what had happened to the cruiser class, the [[Anaxes/Legends|Anaxes]] architects extended their classification system to account for the possibility of truly gigantic warships. [[Corvette/Legends|''Corvettes'']] were fast, light attack ships which were used in a variety of roles, including blockade running, anti-starfighter missions, or escort and support for larger ships. [[Frigate/Legends|''Frigates'']] sat between two hundred and four hundred meters and served the purpose of eliminating smaller vessels of an enemy fleet and often carried their own starfighter squadrons. [[Cruiser/Legends|''Cruisers'']] were from four hundred to six hundred meters in length and were heavily armed relative to their size and could often trade blows with much larger ships. [[Heavy cruiser/Legends|''Heavy cruisers'']] were from six hundred to one thousand meters in length and were typically the backbone of any fleet engagement. [[Star Destroyer/Legends|''Star Destroyers'']] were between one and two kilometers in length and were typically the most numerous large starship, specializing in heavy ship-to-ship combat. [[Battlecruiser/Legends|''Battlecruisers'']] were from two to five kilometers in length and were heavily armed, designed for long-range, independent operations hunting down other capital ships. Finally, [[Star Dreadnought/Legends|''dreadnoughts'']] were ships over five kilometers in length and so powerful that the mere threat of their deployment could pacify multiple sectors.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" /> Although not an official class, there was also a designation known as ''[[superdreadnaught]]'', which included the ''[[Star of Coruscant]]'' and the ''[[Eye of Palpatine]]'' during the [[Great Galactic War]] and the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], respectively, with the implication being that the ships were far larger in size and more powerful than an ordinary dreadnought.<ref name="CotJ">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']]</ref><ref name="The Old Republic">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref>

Additionally, the Anaxes War College System carried a shorthand for use during engagements, one that lumped warships of different classes based on their size and capability. Corvettes, space transports and starships acting as warships in-theater were designated as [[Gunship/Legends|''gunships'']], small, fast, heavily-armed ships that specialized in destroying the maximum number of small enemy ships in a space battle and relied on evasion far more than their shields to escape damage. Frigates and lighter cruisers - the workhorses of most military engagements - were identified as ''cruisers''. Big [[Ship of the line|ships of the line]] whose mere presence could change the course of a battle were referred to as [[Battleship/Legends|''battleships'']].<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

In addition, some capital ships had been developed specifically to both revolutionize space warfare as well as ensure dominance for an extended period of time. A notable example of these ships were the [[Eclipse-class dreadnought|''Eclipse''-class dreadnought]] and the [[Sovereign-class Super Star Destroyer|''Sovereign''-class Super Star Destroyers]] developed by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], and more specifically by the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]].<ref name="Imperial Handbook">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref>

==History==
===The first space battles===
{{Quote|War has always been with us, and will always be with us.|[[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Osvald Teshik]]|<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />}}
[[File:Thanium_star-glaive.png|thumb|left|200px|A [[Thanium star-glaive]] of [[Xim's empire]].]]
Much information surrounding the very earliest wars in space was lost by the era of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], but the legends of the eldest spacefaring civilizations all told an intriguingly similar story – of a terrible war waged with unimaginable weapons.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" /> Such early conflicts included the [[Rakatan revolt|genocidal war]] between the [[Celestial/Legends|Celestials]] and the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]], followed by the savage conquests of the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]].<ref name="Author's Cut">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-the-celestials|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut &mdash; The Celestials|int=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut}}</ref>

In recorded history, starships were first armed as a response to natural hazards: deflector shields were necessary to protected crews and passengers from radiation or micrometeoroids, while ship-mounted laser weapons and missiles were developed in response to rogue asteroids or destructive space-borne creatures. Inevitably, this proliferation of weapons brought space warfare along with space travel.<ref name="HaynesManual">''[[Millennium Falcon Owner's Workshop Manual]]''</ref> The first well-documented wars were those of the [[Tionese (group)/Legends|Tionese]] and the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]]. Tionese warships used guided missiles, torpedo launchers and microwave lasers for offense. Protection was provided by point-defense missiles, clouds of charged particles to diffuse energy weapons, and thin armor plating coated with superconducting, mirror-bright [[Kiirium/Legends|kiirium]] alloy to reflect laser attacks.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

In this era, ships larger than [[Light cruiser/Legends|light cruisers]] were rare: the flagship of [[Xim/Legends|Xim the Despot]], the ''[[Eibon Scimitar]]'', was considered gargantuan in its time, but military historians during the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Period]] generally agreed that it would be considered a [[Heavy cruiser/Legends|heavy cruiser]] at best under the Anaxes War College System.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" /> Wars in this era were fought across networks of jump beacons. Significant conflicts of this early era of space warfare included the [[Cronese Sweeps]], the [[Xim's Expansionist Period|Expansionist Wars]] of [[Xim's empire]], Xim's [[Xim Wars|final war]] with the [[Hutt Empire]], and the [[Unification Wars (Galactic Republic)|Unification Wars]] that founded the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="TEA" />

===Cruiser warfare===
The [[Tionese War]] did not see a shift towards larger warships: such ships were expensive to build and of little strategic use against fleets of cheaper and more nimble craft. [[Alsakan/Legends|Alsakan's]] [[Atgeir-class battlecruiser|''Atgeir''-class battlecruisers]] – renowned for their supposedly impregnable shields – were exceptions to the rule. During the early [[Alsakan Conflicts/Legends|Alsakan Conflicts]], ships like these battlecruisers and [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant's]] ''[[Gilagimar]]'' were chiefly used for home defense while fleets of swift [[Cruiser/Legends|cruisers]] launched raids and protected colonies in the [[Exploitation Region]]. The best example of this was [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Hirken]]'s [[Admiral Hirken's campaign in the Northern Dependencies|Northern Dependencies campaign]] during the [[Fifth Alsakan Conflict]].<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

[[File:FifthAlsakanConflict.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Admiral [[Hirken]]'s defense of the [[Northern Dependencies/Legends|Northern Dependencies]] during the [[Fifth Alsakan Conflict]].]]

Jump beacons were still essential for hyperspace travel, which allowed the [[Bureau of Ships and Services/Legends|Bureau of Ships and Services]] to halt the [[First Alsakan Conflict]] of [[17,018 BBY|17,018]]-[[16,700 BBY]] by threatening to withhold navigational data from both Coruscant and Alsakan. In [[10,966 BBY]], BoSS was also able to end the [[Seventh Alsakan Conflict|Pius Dea Civil War]] by infecting the ships of the [[Pius Dea]] [[Pius Dea|Faithful]] with rogue navicomputer codes that scattered their fleet and left what remained to be easily overwhelmed by a combined [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]-[[Renunciates|Renunciate]] fleet at the [[Battle of Uquine]].<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

After the [[Duinuogwuin Contention]] of [[15,500 BBY]], the Republic encountered few opponents with large warships and so had little use for large capital ships. The [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]] preferred fast gunships that could escort merchant transports and colony ships. The [[Pius Dea Crusades]] of [[12,000 BBY/Legends|12,000-11,000 BBY]] saw the use of [[cathedral ship]]s and large, armored [[Man-of-war/Legends|men-o-war]] optimised for [[Broadside battle|broadside combat]], but the next widespread use of large capital ships came around [[10,000 BBY]] when the Republic was briefly provoked by the rise of the [[Kumauri Empire]]. [[Vall Kumauri]]'s [[Kumauri Battleship|massive battleships]] were armed with [[Mass-driver cannon/Legends|mass-driver cannons]] capable of accelerating [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroids]] to planet-cracking velocities (similar to ancient Hutt ''[[planechanga]]''). The Republic countered with an identical fleet, which cowed or destroyed several hostile civilizations during the Republic's expansion and even served as terror weapons during the [[Osara Mundicide]] of the [[Tenth Alsakan Conflict]]. Advances in [[Planetary shield/Legends|planetary shields]] largely eliminated the threat of bombardment, but the [[Kumauri Empire]]'s most enduring innovation was the use of synthetic [[madilon]] to make smaller, more efficient hyperdrives that allowed longer jumps across the galaxy's network of jump beacons.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

The [[Waymancy Storm]], a furious confrontation between the Galactic Republic and [[Signatories of Waymancy]] in [[7811 BBY]], sparked the next major wave of naval innovation. In the first battles, Republic ships were torn apart by rapid fusillades of laserfire: Waymancy's [[Sisters of the Machinesmith]] had developed the [[Sif-Alulan process]] and produced extremely efficient power generators that allowed for energy weapons far more powerful and with much faster rates than anything the Republic could bring to bear. Waymancy was defeated after the Sif-Alulan process was reverse engineered, allowing the Republic to create its own [[pulse-wave cannon]]s and [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]]. The process was further improved upon by by the [[Verpine/Legends|Verpine]] crafter [[Lyns Skutroo]], who created the [[squintpipe process]] in the 7700s BBY. This created a brief period in which rapid-fire [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolasers]] outclassed all available defenses. This caused naval tacticians to disdain capital ships in favor of swarms of [[Gunship/Legends|gunships]] that could overwhelm opponents. Since [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]] were now useless, this led to a search for stronger hull armor, with [[vacierite]] replacing [[Kiirium/Legends|kiirium]]. In the 7500s BBY, further refinements of the squintpipe process produced shields that were stronger and quicker to regenerate, and shield generators became small enough to be fitted to starships of any size.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

===The golden age of battleships===
The refined [[squintpipe process]] sparked a golden age of warship construction. Capital ships reemerged as the primary warships of the [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic Military]], its [[Planetary Security Forces]], and its enemies, the worst of whom were the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]]. In the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]] of [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], the Republic faced a fleet of massive Sith [[Derriphan-class battleship|''Derriphan''-class battleships]] led by [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow's]] [[Corsair (Derriphan-class)|''Corsair'']]. The Republic Navy countered with ever-larger capital ships, including [[Republic command ship|command ships]], [[Republic battleship (Great Sith War)|battleships]], and the [[Hammerhead-class cruiser|''Hammerhead''-class cruiser]] (one of the most enduring warship designs in galactic history, which remained in military service with upgrades for nearly 3,000 years)<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />
[[File:Battle_of_Vanquo.jpg|thumb|left|250px|''Hammerhead''-class [[Frigate/Legends|frigates]] at the [[Battle of Vanquo]].]]
The double threats of the Sith and the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]] in what became known as the [[Old Sith Wars]] prompted the Republic to build ever-larger, more powerful ships, culminating in titanic clashes between the largest warships yet seen in the galaxy. These included the 3,100-meter [[Inexpugnable-class tactical command ship|''Inexpugnable''-class tactical command ship]], the 1,200-meter [[Centurion-class battlecruiser/Legends|''Centurion''-class battlecruiser]], and the 600-meter [[Interdictor-class cruiser|''Interdictor''-class cruiser]]. This cruiser design projected a simulated [[Gravity well/Legends|gravity well]] into [[Realspace/Legends|realspace]], creating a [[Mass shadow/Legends|mass shadow]] in hyperspace that prevented hyperspace jumps or dragged ships back into realspace. However, this innovation would soon be rendered ineffective by better hyperspace [[Sensor/Legends|sensor]] suites and [[Null quantum field generator/Legends|multiphase null field units]], and it was not until the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] that [[Gravity well projector/Legends|gravity well projectors]] became decisive weapons again.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" /> The [[Great Galactic War]], [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] and [[Galactic War]] saw Republic [[Valor-class cruiser|''Valor''-class cruisers]] and even the "[[superdreadnaught]]" ''[[Star of Coruscant]]'' fighting the [[Terminus-class destroyer|''Terminus''-class destroyers]] and [[Harrower-class dreadnought|''Harrower''-class dreadnoughts]] of the [[Imperial Navy (Sith Empire)|Imperial Navy]] of the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|restored Sith Empire]].<ref name="The Old Republic" />

By [[4100 BBY]], the era of the jump beacon was coming to its end as more effective and powerful [[Navigation computer/Legends|navigation computers]] were developed. Wary of rumblings beyond the Republic frontier, the Republic Navy conducted crash research to ensure that its ships could cross the galaxy quickly and safely without having to rely on beacons. This was a prescient move: during the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]] and the [[Mandalorian Wars]], the Republic Navy destroyed many jump beacons in an effort to deny its enemies easy passage into Republic space.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

Technological innovation slowly obsoleted battleships, however: the [[Seventeenth Alsakan Conflict|Seventeenth and final Alsakan Conflict]] was caused by Alsakan maintaining and expanding its fleet despite the conclusion of the Galactic Wars. The Republic responded by building a fleet of two-kilometer-long [[Invincible-class Dreadnaught Heavy Cruiser|''Invincible''-class fast battleships]]. [[Alsakan/Legends|Alsakan]] and the Axis' response was mass-produced squadrons of [[Axis sublight missile corvette|sublight missile corvettes]], which successfully defended their systems from Republic raids. However, [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] reacted with a fleet of long-range frigates. Technological breakthroughs enabled them to be outfitted with fast engines, strong shields, and heavy turbolasers, allowing [[Prince-Admiral/Legends|Prince-Admiral]] [[Jonash e Solo]] to rapidly outfight both Coruscanti and Alsakani battleships and forcing a [[Alsakan Conflicts peace treaty|peace treaty]] on both.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

===The Ruusan Reformations===
{{Main|Ruusan Reformations/Legends}}
The battleship era ended in the [[2500 BBY/Legends|2500s BBY]] owing to economic concerns. Tacticians once again came to prefer fleets of smaller [[Cruiser/Legends|cruisers]], most notably the striking fleet of [[Wroshyr wood/Legends|wroshyr-framed]] wooden [[Gunship/Legends|gunships]] led by the [[Jedi Lord]] [[Valenthyne Farfalla]] aboard the ''[[Fairwind]]'' in the [[New Sith Wars]]. The [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Ruusan Reformation]] of [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]] halted large battleship construction: not only was the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]] dismantled and responsibility for defense given to the [[Planetary Security Forces]] and the [[Judicial Forces/Legends|Judicial Forces]], but the size of ships was capped at the six-hundred meter [[Cruiser/Legends|cruiser]]. Ships larger than six hundred meters had their hyperdrives limited and their navicomputers restricted to local charts. For centuries after Ruusan, capital ships larger than light cruisers were rare and were seen as extravagant.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

Cruisers emerged as the workhorses of the PSFs and the Judicials alike, and they served well in the [[Unification Campaigns]] after the New Sith Wars. However, as the Republic's authority in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] slowly crumbled in the final centuries of the [[Great Peace of the Republic]], wealthy industrial sectors began building new capital ships for the sector fleets, while megacorps like the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] took advantage of loopholes in the law to develop their own trade defense fleets. These developments culminated in giant cruisers on a scale not seen for millennia, with rich planets like [[Kuat/Legends|Kuat]] and [[Rendili/Legends|Rendili]] seeking to create impregnable defenses and impress their neighbors. Additionally, shipwrights were granted exemptions to allow them to pursue technological innovations and showcase prototype designs. This resulted in corporate "demonstration fleets" made up of variations on warship design, which were often leased to sectors that could afford them. By the [[30 BBY/Legends|30s BBY]], rich sectors were awash with massive warships, with their fleets' numbers swelled by loans from starship manufacturers. Meanwhile, the defense limits of the Ruusan Reformations meant that poor Rim sectors struggled to police their worlds and defeat [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] and [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] with undersized fleets of underpowered warships.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

===The experience of the Clone Wars===
[[File:Spacebattle.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic]] and [[Confederate Navy/Legends|Confederate Navies]] clash at the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|Battle of Coruscant]].]]
The [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] of [[22 BBY/Legends|22]] to [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], a product of the [[Order of the Sith Lords]]' [[Grand Plan/Legends|Grand Plan]] to seize control of the galaxy, fundamentally changed the conduct of space warfare. Most significantly, it resulted in the spread of three new enormous variations of capital ship: the [[Star Destroyer/Legends|''Star Destroyer'']], the [[Battlecruiser/Legends|''Battlecruiser'']], and the [[Star Dreadnought/Legends|''Star Dreadnought'']]. Even prior to the Ruusan Reformation, ships larger than two kilometers in length had been rare, and most warships tended to be below the one-kilometer mark. However, the Clone Wars saw the rapid development and widespread use of Star Destroyers. While the name had originally been a corporate marque of [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards]], it came to refer to a ship in excess of one kilometer long, carrying an armament powerful enough to lay waste to entire [[Star system/Legends|star systems]]. Star Destroyers, exemplified by the [[Venator-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Venator''-]], [[Victory-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Victory''-]], and finally the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class]], would become the backbone of battle fleets during and after the Clone Wars. The Separatists' answer to the Star Destroyer was the [[Providence-class carrier/destroyer/Legends|''Providence''-class carrier/destroyer]], but though the class was made famous by [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]]' [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']], there were relatively few of them.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

An even larger development of capital ship was the battlecruiser, massive, heavily armored warships designed to hunt down and destroy other capital ships in long-range, independent operations. The first warship that gained formal recognition as a battlecruiser was KDY's 2.5-kilometer [[Procurator-class Star Battlecruiser|''Procurator'']], which served as a template for a series of ever-larger KDY battleships. By the time of the Clone Wars, dozens of battlecruisers defended [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core]] and [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies]] sectors, among the ''Procurator's'' refinement, the four-thousand-meter [[Praetor-class Star Battlecruiser/Legends|''Praetor''-class]]. The majority of these huge ships went into Republic service during the Clone Wars, with most serving as local defense against Separatist incursions. Others were uparmored, fitted with transgalactic-capable hyperdrives and became the spearpoints of task forces sent against key Separatist worlds, most notably and tragically the ''[[Quaestor]]'' at [[Pammant/Legends|Pammant]]. The [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] maintained a few ships that could be called battlecruisers, most notably the [[Subjugator-class heavy cruiser/Legends|''Subjugator''-class]], best represented by the [[Malevolence/Legends|''Malevolence'']], but they preferred fleets of smaller [[Frigate/Legends|frigates]] and light destroyers. The [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] would commission relatively few battlecruisers, relegating them to Core defense, and saw them as being less versatile than Star Destroyers but not instilling the same terror as dreadnoughts.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

[[File:ImperialFleetRefueling.jpg|thumb|left|250px|New instruments of naval power: [[Battlecruiser/Legends|Battlecruisers]], [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]] and a [[Star Dreadnought/Legends|Star Dreadnought]] refuelling.]]

The star dreadnoughts were the largest class of capital ship ever built, and were massive warships designed to be so powerful that the mere threat of their deployment would pacify multiple sectors. The first warship considered a dreadnought was KDY's eight-kilometer [[Mandator-class Star Dreadnaught|''Mandator'']], built twenty years before the Clone Wars. It triggered a race among wealthy sectors for similar warships, and during the Clone Wars, KDY developed the improved [[Mandator II-class Star Dreadnaught/Legends|''Mandator'' II]] design. The Galactic Empire continued star dreadnought development, culminating in the [[Sarlacc Project]] and the [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|''Executor''-class star dreadnought]], a 19-kilometer-long battleship so large and powerful that it was nearly invincible in fleet combat. Many in the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]], however, came to disdain star dreadnoughts as inefficient compared to fleets of smaller cruisers for patrolling the galaxy, and derisively referred to them as "[[Super Star Destroyer/Legends|Super Star Destroyers]]."<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

The Republic Navy was opposed by the [[Confederate Navy/Legends|Confederate Navy]], which compensated for the relative fragility of their [[Recusant-class light destroyer/Legends|''Recusant''-class light destroyers]] and [[Munificent-class star frigate/Legends|''Munificent''-class star frigates]] with huge numbers of the [[Droid/Legends|droid]]-crewed vessels, as well as immense swarms of [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]]. In addition to traditional [[Interceptor/Legends|interceptors]] like the [[Belbullab-22 starfighter/Legends|Belbullab-22]] and the [[Droid tri-fighter/Legends|droid tri-fighter]], and [[Bomber/Legends|bombers]] like the [[Hyena-class bomber/Legends|''Hyena''-class]] and [[Belbullab-24 strike bomber|Belbullab-24]], the Separatists also operated large numbers of [[Snubfighter/Legends|snubfighters]]. In a departure from traditional doctrine, the Confederate Navy would often deploy squadrons of snubfighters like the [[Vulture-class starfighter/Legends|''Vulture''-class droid starfighter]] in both a dogfighting an an anti-ship role. Developments in snubfighter technology had outraced doctrine. The performance of [[N-1 starfighter/Legends|N-1 starfighters]] at the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]] had shown the Separatists that hyperspace-capable snubfighters could indeed destroy battleships. The experience was confirmed with the destruction of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] [[Malevolence/Legends|''Malevolence'']] at the [[Battle of the Kaliida Nebula/Legends|Battle of the Kaliida Nebula]], helped in no small part by it being crippled by Y-wing starfighters. The Republic Navy was not slow to notice this. Its main starfighter carriers of the war, the [[Venator-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Venator''-]] and [[Victory-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Victory''-class]] [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]], were originally designed with traditional doctrine in mind and to operate [[NTB-630 naval bomber/Legends|NTB-630 torpedo bombers]] in an anti-capital ship role, alongside short-range [[A-6 Interceptor]]s for escort and dealing with enemy starfighters. By the end of the Clone Wars, carrier capacity was largely given over to snubfighters like the [[Aggressive ReConnaissance-170 starfighter/Legends|ARC-170]], and designers like [[Vors Voorhorian]] and [[Walex Blissex/Legends|Walex Blissex]] spent the war years designing a new generation of snubfighters that could dogfight on equal terms with any starfighter in space.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

The Confederacy of Independent Systems fought the Republic with a [[stateless strategy]], making surgical strikes and terror raids designed to deny the Republic key invasion corridors, undermine support for the war, and sever key fleets' supply lines. The sheer size of Republic territory meant that it was impossible for the Republic Navy to repel all the raids, and if it tried to take the offensive against the Separatists, it might leave key worlds vulnerable. The Republic never found a solution to this strategy. Instead, it outgrew it, conscripting vast numbers of new crews and cloning huge numbers of new [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]], and by the third year of the war, had committed a substantial portion of its much larger industrial base to produce a fleet so large it could both defend its territories and take the fight to the Separatists. The Separatists' Outer Rim holdings were ground down in an attritional campaign known as the [[Outer Rim Sieges/Legends|Outer Rim Sieges]]. After the [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Separatist Droid Army]] was finally [[Mission to Mustafar/Legends|deactivated]], the new [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] inherited the immense [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic Military]] and both the Republic and the Confederacy's military-industrial complexes, allowing [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] to consolidate control over the galaxy with a [[Imperial Navy/Legends|new navy]] larger than anything ever seen before.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

===The Galactic Civil War===
The [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] of [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]]-[[19 ABY/Legends|19 ABY]] cemented the role of the [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] as the central warship of navies. Under Emperor Palpatine, the [[Planetary Security Forces]] were nationalized and merged into the [[Sector Group/Legends|Sector Groups]], massive concentrations of fleet power at the sector level. Distrusting local loyalties, these fleets were rapidly filled with new ships loyal to [[Coruscant/Legends|Imperial Center]] (decommissioned PSF equipment and ships would later become a major source of resources for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebellion]])<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" /> The [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] ultimately expanded to become the largest military starfleet the galaxy had ever seen, peaking at 25,000 Star Destroyers and millions more smaller ships.<ref name="Imperial Sourcebook>''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]''</ref>

[[File:SWA_The_Corellian_Conflict_box_art.png|thumb|right|250px|Forces of the Rebel Alliance and Galactic Empire engage each other in Corellian space]]
The Imperial Navy's doctrine emphasised maximizing capital ship firepower rather than achieving starfighter superiority, and it subordinated its starfighters to this role.<ref name="Imperial Sourcebook" /> As such, the Republic Starfighter Corps, when reorganized into the [[Starfighter Corps (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Starfighter Corps]] of the Galactic Empire, was reduced to being dependent on the Imperial Navy. The large carrier capacity of the [[Venator-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Venator''-class Star Destroyer]] was done away with in future designs in favor of smaller fighter complements. This made room for bigger, more powerful reactors, allowing them to be more heavily armored and carry stronger shields and more powerful weapons, all of which would make starfighters less effective. The new [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] became the backbone of the Imperial Starfleet and was heavily optimised for fleet combat, carrying only a single [[Fighter wing/Legends|wing]] of 72 starfighters, relatively small in comparison to the ''Venator''-class' 420 fighters.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" /> The Imperial Navy's general strategies and functions included blockading ports in order to prevent supplies from reaching a planet to cripple its ability to fight; bombarding planets in order to annihilate its infrastructure; and transporting other branches of the Imperial military to their destination as well as supplying them with space and aerial support after disembarking.<ref name="Imperial Handbook" />

Seeing it as a legacy of the Separatists, the Imperial Navy abandoned snubfighters in favor of more traditional starfighters: the [[TIE series/Legends|TIE Series]], exemplifying traditional starfighter doctrine with the [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN Line Starfighter]] and the [[TIE/sa tactical bomber/Legends|TIE/sa Bomber]], was a series of barebones fighter designs built around a ball-shaped cockpit and the revolutionary [[Twin ion engine/Legends|twin ion engine]] design. Seen as complements to Star Destroyers, they served as escorts, scouts, hit-and-fade raiders, and [[Bomber/Legends|bombers]] supporting ground troops. As such, they lacked [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrives]], [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]], or even life support systems, reducing their mass and giving them great speed and maneuverability, but also limiting their survivability and their range.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" /> The Imperials also chose to eliminate shielding and life-support systems specifically because they viewed the use of such by their [[TIE pilot]]s as cowardice.<ref name="Visual Dictionary" /> In addition, as a holdover towards the Galactic Republic's use of cloned soldiers and pilots during the Clone Wars and their treatment of the clones as living droids, the TIE pilots were also given a notoriously low amount of protection during battle and even during training exercises, even when Imperial officers requested that they make accommodations for the growing amount of human pilots that graduated from the Imperial Academy system, which resulted in the TIE fighter being a symbol for the Empire's callous disregard of its own troops.<ref name="Warfare Author's Cut 10">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-part-10-the-rise-of-the-empire|series=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|text=Part 10: The Rise of the Empire}}</ref>

The Clone Wars had stimulated aggressive new research into [[Interdiction field/Legends|interdiction field]] technology, and the Empire built on the Republic's developments. New designs of [[Gravity well projector/Legends|gravity well projector]] were powerful enough to pull any ship out of hyperspace or to pin it in realspace. However, only large capital ship had the spaceframe and drive systems to carry the large, bulbous generators, and [[Immobilizer 418 Interdictor-class Heavy Cruiser|Immobilizer 418 cruisers]] became common sights in Imperial fleets. They were decisive in preventing the immediate escape of the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance Fleet]] into hyperspace at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]. Owing to their role, however, these cruisers were underpowered for their size, and only large battleships like the [[Sovereign-class Super Star Destroyer|''Sovereign''-class]] and [[Eclipse-class dreadnought|''Eclipse''-class dreadnoughts]] were big enough to carry effective interdictor systems without serious penalties in weaponry.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

The Galactic Empire was opposed by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], which operated on an entirely different military philosophy. Since it lacked large numbers of capital ships, the Rebel Alliance made heavy use of snubfighters as part of its [[stateless strategy]]. Powerful starfighters like the [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing]] conducted [[Hit-and-hype raiding|hit-and-hype raids]] against prominent Imperial targets and supply convoys, using their superior shielding, armament, and hyperdrives to inflict disproportionate damage on Imperial targets. Meanwhile, the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance Fleet]] would roam the galaxy, challenging Imperial authority merely by existing, and waiting for the chance of a decisive battle with the Galactic Empire. The Galactic Empire made belated moves to develop their own snubfighters like the [[TIE Advanced x1/Legends|TIE Advanced x1]] and the [[TIE/d "Defender" Multi-Role Starfighter/Legends|TIE/D Defender]] after the Rebels inflicted humiliating defeats on them with X-wings, but the most numerous new development was the [[TIE/IN interceptor/Legends|TIE/IN]], a non-hyperspace capable traditional [[Interceptor/Legends|interceptor]] that though capable of outracing Rebel fighters, was not equipped with deflector shields. Only declining numbers of [[TIE pilot]]s in the years after Emperor Palpatine's death as the Empire lost ground to the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] spurred [[Warlord/Legends|warlords]] such as [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]] to retrofit TIE Interceptors with shields.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />
[[File:LusankyavsReaper-EGW.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The [[Orinda campaign]] of [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]] reaffirmed the utility of large [[Battleship/Legends|battleships]].]]
A fourth Imperial influence on space warfare was its increasing resort to [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapons]] to counteract the Rebels' [[stateless strategy]]. The Empire's initial response was a policy of reprisal, a system of state terror that was institutionalised in the [[Tarkin Doctrine/Legends|Tarkin Doctrine]].<ref name="Imperial Sourcebook" /> However, the policy of overwhelming force in an effort to deny the Rebels safe haven did more to foment resistance than eliminate it. The creation of superweapons like the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Stars]], the [[Eclipse-class dreadnought|''Eclipse''-class dreadnoughts]], the [[Galaxy Gun]], and the [[Sun Crusher]], was intended to reverse this state of affairs by introducing the possibility of a reprisal so terrifying - namely, the destruction of entire planets, or even entire star systems - that no world would risk aiding the Rebellion.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" /> All these superweapons consumed enormous amounts of resources and more often than not were destroyed early in their lives by concentrated Rebel raids, most notably the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] and the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], by the very snubfighters the Empire had disdained.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope">{{Film|IV}}</ref><ref name="Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi">{{Film|VI}}</ref> The risks of using superweapons were such that, at least regarding the Death Stars, their mere usage required both an Imperial Intelligence report as well as explicit authorization from the Emperor and his office to those with oversector authority.<ref name="Imperial Handbook" />

After the destruction of the [[Death Star II/Legends|Second Death Star]] at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] and the subsequent collapse of Imperial authority, the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] moved away from the development of battlecruisers and dreadnoughts: its strategists saw them as obsolete, narrowly-focused on fleet combat, and vulnerable to "[[Trench Run Defense|trench run disease]]" - starfighters hugging close to their hulls and using surface trenches for cover to launch strafing runs. Ship design in the [[Nebula-class Star Destroyer|Defender]] and [[New Class Modernization Program]]s instead focused on smaller, more versatile, modular ships, as well as a focus on [[Carrier/Legends|fleet carriers]] for large starfighter complements. However, the poor performance of the [[New Republic Defense Fleet/Legends|New Republic Defense Fleet]] against fleets of dreadnoughts in [[Operation Shadow Hand]], and the experience of the [[Lusankya/Legends|''Lusankya's'']] duel with the [[Reaper (Executor-class)|''Reaper'']] during the [[Orinda campaign]], forced a change in design philosophy. The [[Mon Calamari Shipyards/Legends|Mon Calamari Shipyards]] subsequently created the 8.5-kilometer [[Mediator-class battle cruiser|''Mediator''-class battle cruiser]] and the two massive, 17-kilometer [[Viscount-class Star Defender|''Viscount''-class Star Defenders]], [[Bounty (warship)|''Bounty'']] and [[Krakana (Viscount-class)|''Krakana'']], intended as the centerpiece of the New Republic's Outer Rim defenses in the aftermath of the Galactic Civil War.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

===The Yuuzhan Vong War===
[[File:UnknownVongBattle.jpg|thumb|right|250px|[[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] engage the [[Yuuzhan Vong]].]]
The [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] adopted a military system that was wholly different to that of the Galactic Empire. Unlike the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]], which had been focused on invasion and occupation, the [[New Republic Defense Fleet/Legends|New Republic Defense Fleet]] was focused on peacekeeping, patrolling, and rapid crisis response, working with and alongside [[Planetary Security Forces]] rather than absorbing them. To this end, rather than the Imperial Navy's immense number of ships and [[Sector fleet/Legends|Sector Groups]] used to hold down an entire galaxy, the New Republic Navy was smaller and divided into four (later five) large fleets of some five hundred ships each (each roughly the size of an augmented Imperial Sector Group).<ref name="Cracken's Threat Dossier">''[[Cracken's Threat Dossier]]''</ref> The four fleets later became permanent regional commands based at [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], [[Bothawui/Legends|Bothawui]], [[Elom (planet)/Legends|Elom]], and [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]]. The emphasis was on flexibility, with one [[Battle group/Legends|battle group]] in each fleet serving as a mobile reserve which could be reinforced with multi-role [[Task force/Legends|task forces]] to temporarily become a powerful battle fleet.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

This system served the Republic well after [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]], blockading and neutralizing the last Imperial holdouts. However, it meant that the New Republic was woefully unprepared for a totally unexpected threat when the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] began in [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]]. [[Extragalactic/Legends|Extra-galactic]] alien invaders, the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] operated bizarre organic starships and weapons far more powerful than their New Republic equivalents. A single ''[[Yaret-Kor]]'' plasma cannon (the primary armament of most Yuuzhan Vong ships) aboard a ''[[yorik-et]]'' (the primary Yuuzhan Vong starfighter analog, nicknamed the "coralskipper" by New Republic pilots) was noted to have greater firepower than all four [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannons]] aboard an [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing starfighter]]. Nearly all Yuuzhan Vong ships were more heavily armed than their galactic counterparts, though their ability to defend themselves was typically inferior.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

Regardless, the New Republic's fleet organization led to it adopting a strategy of husbanding its fleets, guarding the key hyperspace approaches to the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core]] and [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies]] while it built up its forces in preparation for a decisive fleet battle on ground of its own choosing. The strategy was fundamentally based on a perception of what had allowed the Rebel Alliance to decisively defeat the Empire at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], but it neglected other tactics that had also served the Rebellion, including commerce raiding, pinpoint strikes, and local defense. This made the New Republic appear weak in the early stages of the war, and the obsession with ceding ground in the hopes of luring the Yuuzhan Vong into a decisive engagement meant that great swaths of the galaxy and billions of people were abandoned to the invaders: The Yuuzhan Vong would capture the majority of the territory they would hold during the war in its first year.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" /><ref name="TEA" />

Despite a disastrous first two years of the war which culminated in the [[Battle of Coruscant (Yuuzhan Vong War)|loss of Coruscant]] to the Yuuzhan Vong and the near-destruction of [[Galactic City/Legends|Galactic City]], the New Republic, reorganized into the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]], at last achieved technological parity with the Yuuzhan Vong. Innovations such as "stutter fire" laser cannons to confuse and overwhelm [[dovin basal]] defensive shields and [[Gravitic amplitude modulator|jamming]] [[yammosk]] war coordinators allowed the Galactic Alliance to win more victories, culminating in the [[Battle of Yuuzhan'tar]], where a massive Alliance, [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]], [[Hapes Consortium/Legends|Hapan]], [[Chiss Ascendancy/Legends|Chiss]] and [[New Jedi Order|Jedi]] force descended on occupied Coruscant, killed [[Supreme Overlord]] [[Shimrra Jamaane|Shimrra]] and ended the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]].<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

===After the Vong===
The immense taxes required for reconstruction in the aftermath of the Yuuzhan Vong War soon provoked resentment across the sectors, while others, mindful of the New Republic's failure to defend them during the war, began building up their [[Planetary Security Forces]] to levels that soon caused concern on Coruscant. The [[Sector Defense Limits]] of [[37 ABY]] put ceilings on military forces and capabilities, but provoked even more resentment, nowhere more so than on [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]], a system with a history of prickly independence. Corellian defiance of GA military limits and withholding its reconstruction contributions provoked the [[Second Galactic Civil War]] of [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]]. After the [[Galactic Alliance Defense Force]] continued its efforts to centralize military resources, systems with important shipyards, munitions factories and defense fleets began declaring their independence as well. Led by Corellia, [[Bothawui/Legends|Bothawui]] and [[Commenor/Legends|Commenor]], they formed a breakaway independent [[Confederation]].<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

[[File:Legacy8.jpg|thumb|right|150px|A [[Pellaeon-class Star Destroyer|''Pellaeon''-class Star Destroyer]] fighting with a [[MC140 Scythe-class main battle cruiser|''Scythe''-class battle cruiser]].]]
In the aftermath of the war, the Galactic Alliance increased centralized funding of the Defense Force and reduced its reliance on member worlds for defense. In return for increased taxation, restrictions on member worlds' military forces were loosened. For nearly a hundred years, this bargain kept the galaxy largely peaceful. The numbered fleets gave way to larger named fleets assigned to regions of the galaxy, for example, the [[Colonies Fleet|Galactic Alliance Colonies Fleet]]. Military philosophy would continue to evolve: in the years leading up to the [[Sith–Imperial War]], the Alliance worked to re-establish [[Sector fleet/Legends|Sector Fleets]] to keep member worlds' warships close to their homeworlds.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

Shipbuilding philosophy developed as well. By the start of the [[Sith–Imperial War]] in [[128 ABY]], which saw the resurgence of the [[Fel Empire|Galactic Empire under the Fel Dynasty]] as the main galactic power at the expense of the Galactic Alliance, both sides had abandoned [[Battleship/Legends|battleships]] almost entirely, largely owing to the enormous cost of operating them.<ref name="Legacy Era Campaign Guide">''[[Legacy Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

==Strategy==
===Types of strategy===
{{Quote|Military goals are reached through a combination of originality and brutality.|[[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]]|<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />}}
[[File:SpaceWarfare-SWGMB.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Rebellion starfighters attack Imperial forces including TIE fighters and ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers.]]
The multidimensional battlefield made space warfare operations complex and difficult to master. In addition to the complexities of space combat itself, related operations like logistics and support were equally complex. Strategies in space warfare mirrored those applied on the ground, and included asymmetric, attritional, conventional and psychological strategies.

Asymmetric strategies, for example, the [[stateless strategy]], were often used by belligerents with a numerical disadvantage to their opponents, The various [[Sith Empire (disambiguation)|Sith Empires]] in their endless wars against the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] in its war against the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] all used asymmetric strategies. Such strategies relied on decentralization and the sheer vastness of space to allow a smaller belligerent to beat a larger one. A decentralized power without a clearly-defined homeworld or territory would have to be overcome everywhere it existed before it could be defeated. The vastness of space meant that throughout history, even the largest militaries found controlling space impossible. This gave an advantage to the decentralized belligerent: since the larger opponent could not defend everywhere, the smaller power could choose its battles and strike where its opponent was not. This would force the larger power into making the choice between heavily-defending a handful of key "[[Fortress world/Legends|fortress worlds]]", thus allowing the enemy a free hand elsewhere, or dispersing their forces and so risking the loss of a key [[Planet/Legends|planet]] through defeat in detail. [[Galactic economy|Economic]] considerations and public pressure tended to force states to adopt the fortress world strategy.<ref name="TEA" />

Attritional strategies made use of superior numbers to grind the enemy down, often with large numbers of casualties. Such a strategy was used by the Republic during the [[Outer Rim Sieges/Legends|Outer Rim Sieges]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]: since it possessed territories in its own right, the Confederacy of Independent Systems was vulnerable to being attacked conventionally, and once the Republic's superior industrial base had produced enough [[Warship/Legends|warships]] to both defend their territories and take the offensive, the CIS was slowly ground down to defeat.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

Conventional strategies were used by and against belligerents with defined [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworlds]] and colonies, and involved identifying and attacking significant military objectives to reduce the enemy's territory and military forces. It involved organized military forces seeking to engage each other in formal battles, as opposed to, say, targeting civilian populations. After the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], the Galactic Empire and the New Republic typically fought each other in a conventional fashion.<ref name="TEA" />

Psychological strategies involved boosting the morale of one's own forces while degrading that of the enemy's, or that of their civilians, typically through terror tactics. [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] saw inducing terror in civilian populations to be the very essence of war, and during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] committed atrocities like the release of the [[Brainrot Plague]] in the [[Weemell sector/Legends|Weemell sector]] and the [[Orbital bombardment/Legends|orbital bombardment]] and [[Bombardment of Humbarine/Legends|utter depopulation]] of [[Humbarine/Legends|Humbarine]], which reduced the planet's crust to so much slag.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" /> Terror operations could be a response to the stateless strategy, namely the use of reprisal to scare civilians into denying the enemy safe haven. However, this could do more to foment resentment and resistance than it could to combat it. The Galactic Empire's creation of the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Stars]] and other [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapons]] was intended to reverse such a state of affairs by introducing the possibility of a reprisal so terrifying - namely, the destruction of entire planets - that no world would risk aiding the Rebellion. [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]], meanwhile, was a master of a more subtle form of psychological warfare: at the [[Battle at Ukio|Battle of Ukio]] in [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]], he made use of [[Cloaking device/Legends|cloaked]] Star Destroyers, slipped below the planet's shields while they were down and coordinated with the rest of his fleet by the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Joruus C'baoth]], to make it appear that he could shoot through [[Planetary shield/Legends|planetary shields]], which terrorized the [[Ukian/Legends|Ukians]] into surrendering. Later, at Coruscant, he deployed two dozen cloaked [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroids]] while dry-firing his [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beams]] to fake the launch of three hundred more. These asteroids blockaded the planet, and by threatening the possibility of an asteroid impact or a collision with shipping, Thrawn effectively [[Siege of Coruscant|knocked Coruscant out of the war]] and put it into a permanent state of [[Clone Wars Gambit: Siege|siege]] while dedicating hardly any material to the effort.<ref name="TEA" />

===Astrography and warfare===
[[File:MainGalaxy.png|thumb|right|250px|[[Astrography]] affected the conduct of space warfare more than any other factor.]]
{{Quote|Statistically speaking, the universe is empty. But at faster-than-light speeds, it fills up very quickly.|[[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Pers Pradeux]]|<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />}}
Just as roads and the shape and going of the ground determined where [[Army/Legends|armies]] marched on the surface of planets, so too did [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]] and stellar phenomena like [[Nebula/Legends|nebulae]] determined the movements of fleets. This defined what routes they could take, and what [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] they would have to traverse before reaching those of value. Additionally, while there might be a great many hyperspace routes to and from a target, but statistically speaking, only a few of these route could be traversed quickly, and a military force that controlled the fast routes could rapidly redeploy to intercept an adversary using the slow ones. Hyperspace routes also determined the angle at which an attacking fleet might invade a planetary system, and a defender's options for retreat: the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]] was a costly battle for the Rebel Alliance because the [[Hoth system/Legends|Hoth system]] was located on the decaying [[Ison Trade Corridor/Legends|Ison Corridor]], which was difficult to navigate Rimward and had only two exits, making it easy for the Empire to trap the Rebels in-system, and 17 of 30 evacuating [[Transport/Legends|transports]] were lost to the Imperial [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]].<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

Additionally, control of a point along a hyperspace route enormously influenced military operations in space warfare. If a force controlled a system along a route, then its enemy was separated from the rest of its forces beyond that point. During their advance to the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] from [[4 ABY/Legends|4]]-[[6 ABY/Legends|6 ABY]], the New Republic sought to capture several such points. Admiral [[Firmus Nantz]] and [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian's]] [[Operation on Abraxas|victory]] at [[Abraxas]] kept [[Warlord/Legends|Warlord]] [[Utoxx Prentioch]] fixed within [[Prentioch's Dominion|his territories]] around [[Bomis Koori IV]] and separated him from [[Sander Delvardus]]' [[Eriadu Authority]]. Later, Nantz' [[Battle of Moorja (Galactic Civil War)|capture]] of [[Moorja/Legends|Moorja]] isolated Delvardus and Prentioch from support from the Core while [[Tyr Taskeen]]'s victory at the [[Battle of Glova]] prevented Delvardus from linking up with Imperial forces in the [[Elrood sector/Legends|Elrood]] and [[Minos Cluster/Legends|Minos sectors]]. Isolated from the rest of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], the two warlords were dealt with at the Republic's leisure.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare /><ref name="TEA" />

Control of junctions of hyperspace routes, like [[Yag'Dhul/Legends|Yag'Dhul]] or the [[Mirgoshir hyperspace crossroads]], could be enormously decisive. Control of it would allow a force to continue operations along every hyperspace route emanating from it, and so they were often heavily contested. The Galactic Empire withdrew from the [[Moddell sector/Legends|Moddell sector]] to [[Yag'Dhul/Legends|Yag'Dhul]] in the aftermath of the Battle of Endor to defend against a Rebel drive into the Core from there. After the system was [[Battle of Yag'Dhul (Galactic Civil War)|captured]] by Firmus Nantz in [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]], the entire [[Southern Core]] was effectively at his mercy: he was able to capture the strategic [[Bacta/Legends|bacta]]-producing world of [[Thyferra/Legends|Thyferra]], liberate [[Cilpar]] and [[Mrlsst/Legends|Mrlsst]], and open negotiations with [[Herglic Space/Legends|Herglic Space]].<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" /><ref name="TEA" /> The most significant hyperspace junction in the galaxy was [[Brentaal IV/Legends|Brentaal IV]], the crossroads of the [[Perlemian Trade Route/Legends|Perlemian Trade Route]] and the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]], which therefore controlled access from the Core Worlds to the northern and eastern quadrants. The system was [[Battle of Brentaal IV (New Sith Wars)|captured]] by the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]] during the [[New Sith Wars]], and the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] were only stopped in their march to Coruscant by the [[Army of Light/Legends|Army of Light's]] desperate [[Third Battle of Ruusan|counterattack]] on their supply lines at [[Ruusan/Legends|Ruusan]] under [[Hoth (Jedi Lord)|Lord Hoth]]. It was [[Battle of Brentaal IV (Galactic Civil War)|captured]] by the New Republic's [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]] six months after Emperor [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] death in a celebrated battle, and its capture effectively separated the Empire from its Outer Rim possessions on the Hydian and the Perlemian, leaving the New Republic free to contemplate the conquest of Coruscant.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" /><ref name="TEA" />

The source of a fleet's ships, a [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyard]], was very valuable, and made an important target for an opposing force. As they required ships to defend themselves, shipwrights were also very vulnerable and the attacking fleet would often have to destroy heavy opposition before it could damage the docks. The [[New Republic Second Fleet]]'s campaign in the northern quadrant after [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]] was delayed for nearly two years after Imperial forces [[Battle of the Hast Shipyards|destroyed]] the [[Hast Shipyards|secret shipyards]] at [[Hast]], destroying or damaging nearly thirty New Republic capital ships and derailing the Second Fleet's planned assault on Warlords [[Zsinj]] and [[Treuten Teradoc|Teradoc]].<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

[[Planet/Legends|Planets]] providing strategic material for the war effort were also of paramount importance, because without adequate supplies, after a certain period, any combat [[Starship/Legends|starship]] loses the ability to engage the enemy, either through lack of fuel, lack of munitions, battle damage that cannot be repaired, or the starvation of the crew. Consequently, campaigns could often depend upon cutting the enemy's supply lines, either by attacking its supply ships, or preventing the enemy from reaching their supply ships. If a planet could not be held against an attacking force, then the defender might judge it to be too valuable to be left to the enemy and destroy it. The [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] codenamed such actions "[[Base Delta Zero/Legends|Base Delta Zero]]," defined as "the systematic complete destruction of all 'assets' of production, including factories, arable land, mines, fisheries, and all sentient beings and droids", and was achieved through an [[Orbital bombardment/Legends|orbital bombardment]] that would reduce the upper crust of a planet to slag.<ref name="Imperial Sourcebook">''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]''</ref>

==Tactics==
===Capital ship tactics===
[[File:Naval_style.png|thumb|left|250px|The [[Guarlara (Venator-class)/Legends|''Guarlara'']] and the [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']] in a broadside battle.]]
The strategy adopted by a space navy defined what tactics were used in battle. Some tactics were universal: the most basic tactical principle was to maximize the damage one's fleet did to the enemy while minimizing one's own. Other tactics were more suited to certain strategies: [[space denial]], [[Space-snipe|space-sniping]] and [[hit-and-hype raiding]] were generally best suited for a force pursuing an asymmetric strategy, while [[beambaiting]] might be adopted by an enemy trying to combat that force.

In general [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]] fought other capital ships, and [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] [[Starfighter combat/Legends|fought]] other starfighters. Exceptions included starfighters equipped with [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedoes]] or other warheads, and capital ships, like the [[Lancer-class frigate/Legends|''Lancer''-class frigate]], which were designed to fight starfighters. However, most capital ships were equipped with anti-starfighter cannons to aid their fighter escorts or to serve as the primary defense against fighters in the absence of an escort.

A universal tactic in space battles was maneuvering warships so that they brought more weapons to bear on the enemy than vice-versa, as well as presenting a narrower profile for the enemy to shoot at.<ref name="X-Wing: Wedge's Gamble">''[[X-Wing: Wedge's Gamble]]''</ref>

The Star Destroyer's design meant that it was poorly-optimised for close-range battles, however. Close-range engagements typically resulted in [[broadside battle]]s - two ships flying past each other and firing their side guns into each other's flanks. [[Mon Calamari Star Cruiser/Legends|Mon Calamari Star Cruisers]] were typically better in broadside battles than their Imperial counterparts, since though they did not have as much total firepower as Star Destroyers, they had a much better all-round firing arc.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook">''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]''</ref> Ships optimised for broadside battles might attempt to [[Capping the "T"|cap the enemy's "T"]], namely, engage them while they were in a line-ahead formation so that only the lead ship in the enemy formation could respond. They might even rush straight into the enemy's line in the hopes of breaking it, which typically resulted in a chaotic, close-range [[Brawl/Legends|brawl]] with ships engaging each other in groups of two or three at most.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook">''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]''</ref> The late stages of the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|Battle of Coruscant]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] descended into a close-range brawl between Republic and Separatist ships engaging individually in broadside battles after the [[Open Circle Fleet/Legends|Open Circle Fleet]] arrived and trapped the Separatist invasion force in Coruscant's [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]].<ref name="Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith">{{Film|III}}</ref> However, by [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]] and the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], brawls were sufficiently rare as to be almost unheard-of in space warfare, and it came as a great surprise to [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron]] at Endor when [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Admiral Ackbar]] closed the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance Fleet]] to within a few hundred meters of them to avoid the [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]] of the [[Death Star II/Legends|Second Death Star]].<ref name="Star Wars: Return of the Jedi novelization">[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Star Wars'' Episode VI: ''Return of the Jedi'' (novel)]]</ref> The [[New Republic Defense Fleet/Legends|New Republic Defense Fleet]] later codified such tactics as the [[Ackbar Slash/Legends|Ackbar Slash]].<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook">''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]''</ref>

Long-range and close-range tactics might be combined: the [[Kenobi Offensive]] was such a tactic developed by [[Jedi General/Legends|High Jedi General]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] during the Clone Wars, which involved a series of sniping attacks at range to draw a portion of a larger enemy force out of its formation. Once a defending vessel was destroyed, attacking ships could flood through the gap and attack the enemy force from within.<ref name="The Truce at Bakura Sourcebook">''[[The Truce at Bakura Sourcebook]]''</ref>

The [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Kendal Ozzel/Legends|Kendal Ozzel]] identified three principles in Imperial naval tactics, which he recorded in ''[[Innovations in Imperial Naval Tactics]]''. The first was Surprise, which involved emerging from hyperspace right on top of the enemy. According to Ozzel, the Imperial navigators were capable of pinpoint calculations, which would eliminate the risk of overshooting the target, and thus leave the enemy unable to counter Imperial offensive moves. The second principle was Pursue, where Imperials were to chase the enemy, largely due to the Star Destroyers' great [[Sublight engine/Legends|sublight]] speed. The third was Overwhelm, which involved the entire Imperial force available being used at once, ensuring that the combined firepower would make up for loss of maneuverability. However, [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] implied when reviewing these "innovations" that they were extremely poorly thought out and hardly innovations at all by stating simply, "I can't make fun of this. It's just too easy."<ref name="Imperial Handbook" /> This was confirmed when one of Ozzel's innovations, Surprise, resulted in the Rebel-occupied [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] on [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] bunkering down and generating a deflector shield and buying time for an evacuation, thus forcing the Imperials to enter a [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|costly ground campaign]], an action that resulted in then-[[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] Ozzel's death at the hands of Darth Vader.<ref name="ESB">{{Film|V}}</ref>

[[Interdictor/Legends|Interdictors]] could also play a decisive tactical role in space battles. Since their [[Interdiction field/Legends|interdiction fields]] could either prevent the enemy from escaping or pull them out of [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]], they could pin an enemy fleet where a commander wanted them. Imperial [[Immobilizer 418 Interdictor-class Heavy Cruiser|Immobilizer 418 cruisers]] prevented a Rebel retreat at Endor, and Grand Admiral Thrawn pioneered revolutionary new uses of interdictors during [[Thrawn campaign|his final campaign]]. The [[Thrawn Pincer]] was used by him at the [[Battle of Bilbringi (9 ABY)|Battle of Bilbringi]], and called for interdictor cruisers to create a [[Gravity well/Legends|gravity well]], which denied the enemy an easy escape. Then, reinforcements could jump through [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] into the general area and be pulled out into [[Realspace/Legends|realspace]] by the interdiction field behind the enemy with accuracy and surprise which would otherwise be very difficult to achieve.<ref name="The Last Command">''[[The Last Command]]''</ref> Admiral Ackbar used this same tactic to help defeat the [[Ciutric Hegemony]].<ref name="X-Wing: Isard's Revenge">''[[X-Wing: Isard's Revenge]]''</ref>
